Subject: Operational guarantees and isolation: post-demo clarifications

Hi Emma / Marco —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the clarifying questions we flagged during the demo so we can recommend the right hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

What we heard
- Primary concern: isolation for PHI and predictable latency during batch ingestion windows (you saw token bursts during the demo).
- Target SLO: 99.9% availability and 95th-percentile inference latency under 200ms for the interactive API (typical prompt lengths ~150 tokens).
- Data residency: US-only; retention max 30 days in logs, long-term artifacts kept on customer side.
- Expected steady-state QPS: 60 requests/sec, with scheduled nightly batch jobs that spike to 600 rps for 4–6 minutes.

Questions for your team (answers will change our recommendation)
1) Are those burst windows predictable (cron-based) or ad-hoc?
2) Do you need complete compute isolation (no co-tenants on the same GPU node) or logical isolation + encryption at rest/in-flight is sufficient?
3) Any mandatory certification evidence beyond SOC 2 Type II (e.g., customer audit, custom attestations)?

Preliminary recommendation (based on today's call)
- If you need strict single-tenant compute for PHI and guaranteed P95 latency during bursts: Dedicated reserved capacity with pinned pools (we can size a dedicated pool and reserve headroom for bursts).
- If logical isolation + strong access controls and manageable burst windows: Hosted API with dedicated routing policies + autoscale and burst tiering can meet economics and still provide SLAs.
- Private VPC/on-prem is an option if you require private control plane or air-gapped operations; this has longer lead time and licensing model.

Attached: demo notes and the one-pager on isolation options.

Next steps I propose
- You share answers to the three questions above (1–2 sentences each) by end of day Thursday.
- We'll scope a short Dedicated POC (2–3 day perf validation) if you want to validate burst behavior; Karthik can draft sizing options.
- If you prefer Hosted first, Jordan will put together an SLO/cost comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated for your traffic profile.

Would you like us to schedule the POC kickoff next week?

Thanks —

Thanks Jasmine — added a few technical notes and an initial sizing ask. Attaching a short one-pager with the three recommended deployment checks.

Technical clarifications:
- Latency target: P95 < 200ms for interactive prompts at 150 tokens is feasible on Dedicated with NVLink-backed GPUs and pinned KV cache. On Hosted we can meet that most of the time but need to limit worst-case co-tenant impact unless we add isolation guards (dedicated instances or higher priority routing).
- Bursts: 600 rps for 4–6 minutes is small-medium; we need to know whether the bursts are predictable. For predictable nightly windows we can pre-warm KV cache and autoscale; for ad-hoc spiking we should size a dedicated burst pool (or commit to a Dedicated baseline and use Hosted for overflow).
- Data residency & retention: we support US-only regions and can enforce log retention at 30 days. For PHI: recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS if you need proof-of-separation and key custody.

To size a Dedicated pool I need the following (can be quick bullets):
1) average and 95th percentile prompt length (tokens) for interactive flows and for batch jobs
2) concurrency per user session (typical interactive parallelism)
3) batch job concurrency and whether batching is tolerant to queuing (e.g., 2–5s queue okay?)
4) maximum allowed cold-start window (if any)

If they want, I can prepare two profiles: a Dedicated baseline with reserved GPUs + pre-warm strategy, and a Hosted+Burst hybrid (hosted normal lane + reserved burst nodes).

Attachment: isolation-options-onepager.pdf

Thanks both — quick answers below so you can sketch the POC sizing: 

1) Bursts are scheduled: nightly reconciliation job at 02:00–02:10 PT (cron), plus an end-of-day bulk import at 20:00 PT that lasts ~5–7 minutes. Both are predictable.
2) For PHI we need compute isolation (no co-tenants on the same GPU). Logical isolation + encryption is not acceptable for the reconciliation pipelines — interactive UI can be more flexible.
3) SOC 2 Type II is sufficient for the initial POC; if we advance to production we will require a proof package and access to audit logs for the Dedicated pool.

Sizing quick answers: interactive median ~120 tokens, p95 ~230; interactive concurrency ~40; batch jobs send ~12k requests spread across the 5–7 minute window (roughly 600 rps as you noted). Queuing up to 3 seconds for batches is acceptable.

Yes to a Dedicated POC — can we start the week of July 29? We will need an NDA in place before exchanging full data samples (PHI).

—Emma
